steps.text: Gather ingredients and preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C).
Mix ancho chile powder, white and brown sugars, salt, black pepper, cumin, dry mustard, cayenne, and chipotle pepper in a small bowl until combined.

Place rib rack, meat-side down, on heavy-duty aluminum foil. Prick back of the rack several times with a knife. Generously apply a coating of dry rub to all sides of the rack. Store any remaining dry rub in an airtight container for future use.
With the meat facing down, fold foil around the rack to create a tight seal. Transfer to a sheet pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until tender and cooked through, about 2 hours. Remove and cool 15 minutes.
Increase oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Open foil, drain and discard any accumulated juices and fat. Brush barbeque sauce on all sides of the rack.

Turn the rack on the foil so the meat is facing up. Return to the oven, leaving the foil open and bake for 10 minutes. Remove from the oven and brush another layer of barbeque sauce on the meat side only. Repeat baking and brushing with sauce 4 more times, for a total of 50 minutes baking time.
Cut rack into individual rib segments and serve with more barbeque sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven-Baked Baby Back Ribs
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's oven-baked baby back ribs are seasoned with a homemade dry rub, then glazed with barbeque sauce and baked until tender and delicious. No grill required!

video.description: See how easy it is to make flavorful ribs in the oven.

review.reviewBody: This is a 10 star recipe - the best & easiest method to make ribs. As indicated - use your favorite dry rub and your favorite BBQ sauce but use this low and slow method. For make ahead 'ready to BBQ Ribs' I usually coat the ribs in the dry rub and wrap tightly and let sit in the refrigerator over night. Bake at 250 for at LEAST 2 hours - sometimes they take longer. Then I let them cool in the package - drain the juices out of the package and store in the refrigerator until we are ready to grill. Finishing them on the grill, using indirect heat is so easy and there is virtually no clean up other than to wipe your chops and toss the bones. Enjoy!

My daughter, wife and 93 year old grandma, all said it was one of the top meals that I've made from this site. Applied a sweet smoker rub, that was close to the seasoning ingredients, after I applied a thin yellow musterd to the ribs to hlep the rub stick. Used original $2 sweet Baby Ray's barbecue sauce. Make sure to remove the silver skin from the underside of the ribs. I found the butter knife paper towel method Works easiest

I've made this recipe twice, and its soooo good and easy! I halved the amount of salt and cayenne, added 2 tsp. of garlic powder, and did remove the membrane. Next time I'll half the spice ingredients because I had alot of it left over. Also I only coated the ribs once w/ sauce and cooked at 350 for 15 mins. They were absolutely delish! Paired them with cornbread, black eyed peas, and creamed spinach.

Yes, my husband is a rib connoisseur and he loved these. I did also remove all the membrane. I also used just plain chili powder as that is what I had. I cut the salt to less than half the recipe called for and used seasoning salt. I added a 2 teaspoons of dry mustard and 1 teaspoon of onion powder. Since I used light brown sugar I added a couple of teaspoons of paprika for deeper color and am considering smoked paprika next time. Sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce is terrific on them. Thank you so much! BTW make a double or triple batch and keep in a sealed container in your pantry for the next time, or maybe chicken?

I used kosher salt instead of table salt, and didn't have chipotle powder, but some sweet Hungarian paprika filled in for it well. That rub took the entire bottle of ancho powder. The whole bottle. I won't do that again. It's too pricey, when I can use a premade rub for less than half the cost of that ancho powder alone. It's a little annoying that it didn't make the amount of rub I needed instead giving me a lot extra for another day. I don't need extra. I'd rather have had just what was needed for this recipe itself. The ribs had a nice flavor from the rub on the outside, but it didn't permeate the meat. I liked the carmelization of the sauce and much prefer a sauced rib than a dry one. These were done, and while they were tender, they were not falling-off-the-bone tender, and they were missing that traditional smoke flavor from the grill/smoker. The next time, I'd bake this another hour before even starting to baste them. Our rack of baby back ribs was very meaty so perhaps your results may differ.

Cooking time at 250 degrees was to short for my ribs. Meat didn't pull clean off the bone and they were tough. Next time will increase cooking time to 3 hours before saucing. I did pull the membrane off and used my own dry rub recipe so can't comment on that. Clean up was easy with almost everything contained in the foil.

Great cooking method that delivers juicy, delicious ribs. I used this dry rub recipe as written and, it will leave about a cup of leftover dry rub for another time. Just a personal choice for my bbq flavor preference I will leave out/reduce cumin next time. Top wasn't getting the sticky thick top I wanted so I bumped temp to 425 (same temp I use to finish my bbq chicken thighs) and, it turned out perfectly. No more messy grill to clean. This cooking method is very good! You can use your favorite bbq sauce recipe or tweak a store-bought -- the ribs will turn out great and, no messy grill to clean!

The results of this recipe are first-rate. Although I’ve been smoking ribs outdoors for a few decades now, sometimes the weather just doesn’t cooperate, especially here in New England. These oven-baked ribs are a legitimate alternative! My only changes were to use yellow mustard as a binder to hold the rub on and to remove the silverskin from the back of the racks before applying the rub. For three very mesty racks, it took about 3 hours to reach an internal temperature of 180 degrees (F) while baking at 250 degrees. I then cranked the heat up to 350 and did 3 x 15-minute rounds of saucing and baking, which produced my preferred level of doneness with a slight bark and chew (as opposed to “fall-off-the-bone”). The final internal temperature of the racks was ~190 degrees (F). Thanks for posting!
Love them -- my only major variance is the time. I havent used a thermo but they came out perfect about 4 to 5 hrs b4 pasting n basting. Today I will used my thermo set at 195 and see.
Cooked at 225 on convect for 4.5 hours and left in turned off oven another hour. Moved to grill and cooked over foil (after searing both sides first) for additional 20 min. basting every 10 min.

I mixed about a tablespoon of honey with an 1/8 cup dijon mustard and brushed the ribs first with this before sprinkling on the rub because I didn't have any dried mustard on hand. Followed the rest of the recipe and the ribs were seriously fabulous. Plan ahead; this recipe is about a 4-hour process start to finish.
First time making ribs and they were easy to make and delicious!
No changes, tastes great every time!
I adjust the rub mix to fit my mood. Options include …turbinado sugar, ground cardamom, garlic powder, dried and ground habaneros or scotch bonnets.
A ridiculous amount of rub for one rack of ribs! Half cup if sugar, quarter cup of salt and it tasted like it.
First time making this. The flavor was good. Will make again.
Great flavor and ribs were tender! Making it for the third time!
This is the only way I make ribs, and my picky husband loves them!! Great recipe!
This a foundation recipe I make every month
Yes you're so right ribs need to have a little bite to them I'm so glad you knew this thanks for this great recipe
